Location: Palmerston, Northern Territory
Employment type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: $67,510 to $70,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 91 213 951 452) is a takeaway food outlet located in a busy shopping centre food court in Palmerston. They serve a range of freshly prepared takeaway products, including loaded chips, fish and chips, fried chicken, seafood baskets, hotdogs, ice cream and milkshakes.

They are seeking a reliable and hardworking Kitchenhand to support their food preparation and service team.

About the Role
The Kitchenhand will assist with basic food preparation, maintain clean and hygienic kitchen and service areas, wash utensils and equipment, receive supplies and support the preparation and service of takeaway food.

The position involves standing for extended periods, working in a fast-paced environment and safely handling kitchen equipment, cleaning products and food supplies.

The successful applicant must be available across a rotating roster, including weekends, public holidays and evening shifts where required.

Key Responsibilities
- Clean kitchen, food-preparation, storage and service areas. 
- Wash and sanitise cooking equipment, utensils, containers and other kitchen items.
- Assist with preparing ingredients for cooking and service.
- Portion, assemble and pack food items for customer orders.
- Assist with preparing simple menu items under direction.
- Cook, toast or heat simple food items in accordance with workplace procedures.
- Prepare takeaway packaging, food trays and service materials.
- Receive, transfer, weigh, check and correctly store food supplies.
- Rotate stock and assist with monitoring expiry dates and stock levels.
- Dispose of waste, clean bins and maintain waste-storage areas.
- Maintain clean floors, benches, sinks, fryers and other work areas.
- Assist kitchen and counter staff during busy service periods.
- Follow food-safety, allergen, hygiene and workplace health and safety procedures.
- Report equipment faults, stock shortages and safety issues to the supervisor.
- Complete opening, closing and cleaning duties as allocated.

Skills and Experience
The successful applicant must have:
- Previous experience as a Kitchenhand, food-preparation assistant or in a similar takeaway, hospitality or food-service role;
- Knowledge of basic kitchen hygiene and food-safety practices;
- The ability to follow instructions and workplace procedures;
- The ability to safely use cleaning products and basic kitchen equipment;
- Good attention to cleanliness and food-handling requirements;
- The physical capacity to stand for extended periods and perform repetitive manual duties;
The ability to work efficiently during busy service periods;
Good teamwork and communication skills;
A reliable and punctual approach to work; and
Availability to work weekends, public holidays and shifts according to the business roster.
A food-handling or food-safety certificate is desirable. Relevant workplace training may be provided.
How to Apply
To apply, submit the following:

Resume outlining your work experience and references.
A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
Why you are applying for this position; and
An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.
* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a busy and growing takeaway food business serving the Palmerston community, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026

You will be responsible for ensuring the planning, directing, organising and sourcing of manpower and equipment to ensure clients operational activity is undertaken. Monitor performance to identify and implement improvements to achieve maximum operational efficiency and customer focus. Achieves agreed business goals and objectives whilst consistently ensuring expenditure is maintained in line with budget.

The main activities and accountabilities of this role include but are not limited to:
1. Ensure that all operations are performed in a professional, efficient, safe and cost-effective manner to provide quality service to the client
2. Ensure that all equipment, plant and substances used are suitable for the task and are kept in good working order. This includes the regular maintenance and servicing of equipment which will require close liaison with the workshop/maintenance
3. Monitor department’s performance to ensure service quality standards are being maintained; identify any areas for improvement and discuss recommendations with Management
4. Maintain close liaison with operational supervisors and coordinators to ensure full awareness of project progress and problems. Ensure high quality service is continually provided to achieve both the project and client performance indicators

1. 10+ years industry experience within the Operational environment
2. Technical qualification
3. Previous Supervisory/Management experience

Greenwood Leather is a proudly Australian, family-run maker of fine leather bags and accessories. Since 2016 we have followed a simple passion to craft leather pieces that people genuinely love. Every wallet, handbag and travel bag is handmade and one of a kind, blending old-world craftsmanship with fresh, considered design. Our products are made from the heart, and each carries its own name. Together they form “families” of designs meant to be companions for life pieces that soften, age and gain character with everyday use, gathering the stories of the journeys and people they travel with. Choosing a Greenwood piece means joining our family: customers who value quality over passing trends and who have a soft spot for individual, unconventional style. Based in Cranbourne West, Victoria, we are a growing brand with big ambitions for how our story reaches the people who will love it. That is where you come in.

Key Responsibilities
•	Plan and carry out market research and brief external specialists where needed to uncover fresh opportunities for both our established bag families and any new pieces or accessories we are considering.
•	Study buyer demand and the wider leather-goods and fashion market, gathering and interpreting sales figures, customer data and other statistics to guide where the brand heads next.
•	Guide decisions across the full marketing mix our product range, pricing, promotions and advertising, sales activity, and the retail and online channels through which our products reach customers.
•	Help drive the growth of the business by shaping, documenting and delivering clear marketing objectives, plans and programs, and tracking how well they perform against our goals.
•	Translate customer and market insight into positioning and messaging that stays true to Greenwood’s handcrafted, story-led identity.
•	Develop and manage campaigns across our website, email, social media and other digital channels to build brand awareness and lift online and in-store sales.
•	Monitor competitors, seasonal trends and emerging channels, and recommend practical ways for Greenwood to respond and stand out.
•	Work closely with the design and production side of the business so that marketing activity reflects the true craftsmanship and unique character of each product.
•	Measure the results of marketing spend and report on performance, using what we learn to sharpen future activity and improve return on investment.
•	Support the customer experience from launches and content to promotions and events so that every touchpoint reinforces the feeling of joining the Greenwood family.

What You’ll Bring
•	A Bachelor degree or higher qualification (AQF level 7 or above) in marketing, business, communications or a related field.
•	At least one year of relevant experience in a marketing role.

Personal Attributes
•	Creative and curious you enjoy finding new angles and telling a story well.
•	Organised and self-motivated, able to juggle several projects and meet deadlines.
•	A natural collaborator who works warmly with a small, tight team.
•	Detail-oriented, with pride in doing things properly.
•	Adaptable and hands-on, happy to roll up your sleeves in a growing business.
•	Aligned with our values authenticity, craftsmanship and individuality over chasing every trend.

Hours, Pay & How to Apply:

Employment type: Full-time, approximately 38 hours per week.

Salary:  $95,000 – $105,000 per annum, plus superannuation.

Location: Cranbourne West, VIC.

If you love the idea of helping a heartfelt Australian brand grow, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a short cover letter telling us why Greenwood Leather is the right fit for you.

## Chief Information Officer
## Position Overview
We are looking for a visionary and commercially astute Chief Information Officer (CIO) to lead our organisation's information and communications technology strategy, operations, and governance. This is a senior executive role suited to an experienced technology leader who thrives at the intersection of business strategy and digital innovation. The successful candidate will be responsible for aligning ICT capabilities with organisational priorities, driving transformation, and ensuring the long-term integrity and security of our technology infrastructure.
## Key Responsibilities
- Analyse organisational information needs and define technology solutions that effectively support business objectives and operational performance
- Formulate, implement, and continuously refine ICT strategies, policies, and plans that align with the organisation's broader mission and priorities
- Lead the selection, procurement, and installation of ICT systems and infrastructure, ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and fit for purpose
- Direct ICT operations across the organisation, setting clear priorities between system development, ongoing maintenance, and day-to-day operations
- Oversee the organisation's cybersecurity posture, ensuring robust protections are in place to safeguard data, systems, and digital assets
- Drive digital transformation initiatives that improve organisational efficiency, enhance service delivery, and support innovation
- Develop and manage the ICT budget, ensuring effective allocation of resources and demonstrable return on technology investment
- Build, mentor, and lead high-performing ICT teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous learning, and professional development
- Engage and manage relationships with external technology vendors, partners, and service providers to ensure contractual obligations and service standards are met
- Champion the rollout of user training programmes to ensure staff are equipped to effectively adopt and utilise ICT systems and tools
- Provide executive-level reporting and strategic advice to the Board and senior leadership team on technology risks, opportunities, and performance
- Ensure ICT systems and practices remain compliant with relevant legislation, industry standards, and data governance frameworks
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline
- Demonstrated experience in a senior ICT leadership role, with a strong track record of delivering enterprise-wide technology strategy
- Proven ability to align ICT capability with organisational strategy and drive measurable business outcomes
- Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, risk management, and data governance best practices
- Experience managing large-scale ICT budgets, procurement processes, and vendor relationships
- Excellent leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain high-performing teams
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with a strategic mindset and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
- Sound knowledge of ICT infrastructure, cloud environments, enterprise systems, and emerging technologies
- High-level communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills across all levels of an organisation
## Preferred Qualifications
- Postgraduate qualification in Business Administration (MBA), Information Technology, or a related field
- Industry certifications such as ITIL, TOGAF, CISSP, or equivalent
- Experience leading digital transformation programmes within complex or large-scale organisations
- Familiarity with Australian data privacy legislation, including the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles
- Prior experience presenting to executive leadership teams or Boards of Directors
## Why Join Us?
- Play a pivotal role in shaping the digital future of a dynamic and growing organisation, with genuine influence at the executive level
- Access to ongoing professional development opportunities, including leadership programmes, industry conferences, and certifications
- Flexible working arrangements that support a healthy work-life balance
- Collaborative and inclusive workplace culture that values innovation, integrity, and continuous improvement
- Competitive remuneration package with performance-based incentives and additional employee benefits
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

About the Business:
The Trustee for Maheshvara Family Trust operates a well-established restaurant business in Numurkah, Victoria, specialising in the preparation and service of high-quality meals in a welcoming community setting. Committed to delivering exceptional dining experiences through fresh ingredients, authentic flavours, and consistent standards, the business has built a strong local reputation for reliability and customer satisfaction. Core values centre on integrity, teamwork, food safety, and a genuine passion for hospitality, fostering a supportive and collaborative workplace culture where staff are encouraged to grow, contribute ideas, and take pride in delivering outstanding service to the local community.
About the Position:
This full-time Cook role is vital to the smooth and successful operation of the restaurant, with responsibility for preparing and cooking a variety of menu items to the highest standards of quality, taste, presentation, and food safety. The Cook will work as part of a close-knit kitchen team, contributing to efficient service delivery and helping maintain the business’s reputation for excellence in every dish served.
Key Responsibilities:
Examine ingredients to ensure their quality and suitability before preparation.
Regulate the temperature of ovens, grills, fryers and other cooking equipment.
Prepare and cook meat, poultry, seafood, vegetables, rice, pasta, sauces and other menu items.
Season food during preparation and cooking to achieve the required taste and presentation.
Portion food, arrange dishes and add sauces, garnishes and other finishing elements.
Prepare food to meet customers’ dietary requirements, allergies and special requests.
Follow established recipes, portion-control standards and presentation guidelines.
Monitor food supplies and advise management when ingredients or kitchen items need to be ordered.
Receive and inspect food deliveries and ensure products are properly stored and rotated.
Maintain appropriate stock levels and minimise food spoilage and wastage.
Assist with planning menus and developing new dishes when required.
Prepare ingredients by washing, peeling, cutting, marinating and measuring.
Maintain cleanliness and hygiene across cooking stations, equipment and food-storage areas.
Follow food-safety procedures, including temperature control, date labelling and prevention of cross-contamination.
Train and provide guidance to kitchen assistants and junior kitchen employees where required.
Work closely with chefs, kitchen staff and front-of-house employees to ensure orders are prepared accurately and on time.
Comply with workplace health and safety requirements and report hazards, equipment faults or incidents.
Perform other reasonable kitchen-related duties as directed by the Head Chef or Restaurant Manager.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Commercial Cookery.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in food preparation, cooking techniques, and maintaining kitchen hygiene and food safety standards.
Excellent organisational skills with the ability to work efficiently under pressure and manage multiple tasks.
Good communication and teamwork skills to collaborate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff.
A positive, reliable attitude and commitment to delivering high-quality customer-focused service.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
